title: storing an override setting guesses the defaults of exudyn.config, and the dialog cannot store at all
author: Claude-JG
description: Storing an override setting has three defects, all of them about not knowing the defaults. (1) overrideSettings.Store(config=exudyn.config) stores every value that is not '', 0 or False, because exudyn.config has NO defaults anywhere: it is a facade over globals, so a freshly constructed Config reports the CURRENT values - measured, after exu.config.outputPrecision = 12 a new one says 12 - and the trick every settings structure uses (type(structure)()) cannot work. So it guesses, and it stores settings a user never changed. The maintainer on 2026-09-26: 'you have to improve the config mechanism (could add a Get/Set dict access or so, and also the defaults)'. (2) the settings dialog's 'diff to default' does not say what a user needs once an override file exists: a stored setting is a difference to the default and is listed as one, with nothing to say it is already stored. The maintainer decided the dialog shows the difference to the REAL default and names the settings the file already covers separately, with a comment between them, because comparing against default-plus-override would hide exactly the settings this file is about. (3) there is no way to keep a look from inside the dialog without switching storeDialogPositions on: a 'Store settings' button belongs where a user already is when they decide they like what they see, applying only to visualizationSettings and dialogs, clearly written in the pop-up hints. It writes to the home directory from one click, so it shows exactly what it will write and asks first. revision2026b step RG12.11.
releaseNotes: exudyn.config has a dictionary interface and its defaults: GetDictionary(), SetDictionary(d) and GetDefaults(). The defaults are SNAPSHOTTED during module import, because they cannot be constructed - ExudynConfig is a facade over globals, so a second one reports the current values - and what Exudyn starts with is the default, taken while it still is. The settings are listed once, in configSettings in Pybind_manual_classes.cpp, with the three read-only ones marked, so a new setting reaches the dictionary, the defaults and everything comparing against them; Main/Config.h stays free of pybind11, as eight translation units include it. overrideSettings.Store(config=...) now stores what differs from GetDefaults(); it used to store every value that was not '', 0 or False, which stored settings a user never touched - printToConsole from every run, and outputPrecision because 6 is not 0. The settings dialog has a 'store settings' button: it writes the visualizationSettings that differ from the defaults and the dialog's own size and position, nothing else, and it shows exactly what it will write with a store/cancel pair before writing - one click reaching the home directory. It stores the geometry whether or not storeDialogPositions is on, because that flag is about remembering on closing and this is a user asking. 'diff to default' stays a difference to the real default, and the settings the override file already stores are named again under a comment line saying so: comparing against default-plus-override would hide exactly the settings that file is about. The grouping is GUI.SplitStoredFromChanged, a function, so it is tested without opening a window; the geometry parser became GUI.StoreGeometryString, used by both writers. Eleven new tests.
